messages:
Alicia: Heads up - scanner flagged CVEs in our base images across arches (Alpine arm64: OpenSSL vuln, Ubuntu 22.04: glibc CVE). Need prioritization + rollout plan.

Alicia: scan snippet:
```
Alpine-arm64: openssl 3.0.8 -> CVE-2026-XXXX (HIGH)
Ubuntu-jammy: libc6 2.35 -> CVE-2026-YYYY (CRITICAL)
```

Jordan: Ack. Do we have repro steps for the libc exploit? @Sam any quick try in staging?

Sam: I can run a quick PoC in staging today. Assigning to me. Will also run the distro-provided patches to confirm fix.

Irene: +1 on staging PoC. Note: Alpine uses musl; the glibc CVE only affects Ubuntu images, but OpenSSL on Alpine can still break TLS termination paths.

Leo: For Alpine, there's a patch in the edge repos and a backport in the community channels. Prefer doing a full rebuild with the updated openssl package rather than adhoc lib installs.

Alicia: Proposed plan (high level):
1) Snapshot current base images and tag as archived (archive/*).
2) Build patched base images for amd64 and arm64 with pinned package versions.
3) Sign images (KMS/HSM) and push to staging registry.
4) Canary deploy to staging-canary (5% traffic) for 24h + run E2E/chaos.
5) If canary passes, roll to prod with rolling update and monitor.
Owners: Sam (rebuild PR), Jordan (canary run/monitor), Irene (post-deploy tests), Leo (release signing + SBOM).

Sam: I'll open a PR with a CI job to rebuild images. Proposed tag names: base:ubuntu-22.04-glibc-2.35-patch2026-03 and base:alpine-3.18-openssl-3.0.8-fix.

Jordan: Scheduling: Canary window 2026-04-05T18:00Z -> 2026-04-06T18:00Z. deploy-bot will watch and post status.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for image base:ubuntu-22.04-glibc-2.35-patch2026-03 on cluster staging-canary (deployment id d-98342) :rocket:

Irene: Canary test checklist (quick):
- smoke endpoints return 200
- auth flows full E2E
- latency P95 stays within SLO (compare baseline)
- memory and CPU regressions (container metrics)
- run libc-linked binary fuzz harness (s2i) for 1h on canary nodes

Sam: CI job snippet for PR:
```yaml
name: rebuild-base-images
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  rebuild:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: ./scripts/rebuild_base.sh --image alpine --openssl 3.0.8
      - run: ./scripts/rebuild_base.sh --image ubuntu --glibc 2.35-patch
      - run: ./scripts/generate_sbom.sh --output sbom/
      - run: ./scripts/sign_and_push.sh --kms-key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKey-1
```

Leo: Two additional notes: update SBOMs and SLSA provenance in the release, and ensure the registry manifest includes the signable provenance. Also add a specific arm64 long-run canary (48h) because behaviour diverges on edge nodes.

Jordan: If canary fails the automated checks we have an auto-rollback policy to previous compatible image and we open an incident. Make sure runbooks are linked.

Alicia: Risk summary: the glibc CVE is CRITICAL for user-space exploits on Ubuntu-based images (priority: stateful/back-end services). Alpine OpenSSL is HIGH risk and impacts TLS paths (priority: ingress/services that terminate TLS).

Irene: Also: KMS note — can we use our HSM-backed KMS key for image signing? I will file a ticket to rotate the key and confirm access for CI runners.

Sam: I'll include the KMS key id in the PR and make signing a required step in the rebuild pipeline.

Alicia: Action items captured:
- Sam: open rebuild PR + CI + SBOM + sign (ETA 1 day)
- Jordan: run canary + monitoring dashboards + rollback hooks (ETA canary window)
- Irene: file KMS rotation + prov/docs (ETA 2d)
- Leo: ensure provenance + arm64 long-run canary (ETA 2d)

Alicia: Thanks — I'll post a brief infra announcement when canary starts. :thumbsup:
